safi-cedvel:1-3.t:
* I'rab:
(عن سبيل) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to (صدّوا), and the fāʿil (agent) of (أضلّ) is a pronoun referring to the Name of Majesty (الله). The clause «الذين كفروا ... أضلّ» has no grammatical position, being an opening clause (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين); the clause «صدّوا ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the ṣila clause; and the clause «أضلّ ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (الذين).
2- The (الواو) is a conjunction in all three places. (بما) is attached to (آمنوا), and the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (على محمّد) is attached to (نزّل). The (الواو) is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) - or parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya). (من ربّهم) is attached to an omitted word, a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هو) «[Note: or it is attached to (بالحقّ).]». (عنهم) is attached to (كفّر) ...
The clause «الذين آمنوا ... كفّر عنهم» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the opening clause.
The clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين); the clause «عملوا ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the ṣila clause; the clause «آمنوا (الثانية)» (the second «آمنوا») has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the ṣila clause; the clause «نزّل ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما); the clause «هو الحقّ ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the nāʾib fāʿil «[Note: or it has no grammatical position, being parenthetical.]»; the clause «كفّر عنهم ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين آمنوا); and the clause «أصلح ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause «كفّر».
3- (ذلك) is a demonstrative, a mubtadaʾ, in the position of nominative ...
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أنّ الذين كفروا اتّبعوا) is in the position of genitive through the preposition «bāʾ», attached to an omitted word that is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ذلك); and the interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الذين آمنوا اتّبعوا) is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the first interpreted maṣdar. (من ربّهم) is attached to a ḥāl from (الحقّ). (كذلك) is attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governing verb is (يضرب). (للناس) is attached to (يضرب) ..
The clause «ذلك بأنّ الذين ... » has no grammatical position, being a causal explanation of what precedes; the clause «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين); the clause «اتّبعوا ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the first (أنّ); the clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين) (the second); the clause «اتّبعوا الحقّ ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the second (أنّ); and the clause «يضرب الله ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya).

* Morphology:
(محمّد) is a proper noun derived from الحمد (praise), from the quadriliteral-form verb (حمّد); it is on the pattern of the passive participle, its wazn being مفعّل, with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
The implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya): in the words of the Exalted «أَضَلَّ أَعْمالَهُمْ».
Here their deeds are likened to a stray camel that is neglected, having no master to guard it and care for its affairs; or he made them lost in their disbelief and sins and overwhelmed by them, as water is lost in milk.

safi-cedvel:4-6.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) links what follows it to what precedes it by the tie of causation (al-sababiyya). (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition, attached to (ضرب) «[Note: it may be attached to the implied verb that governs (ضرب).]». (الفاء) links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (ضرب) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, the maṣdar standing in for its verb in the imperative. (حتّى) is a particle of commencement (ḥarf ibtidāʾ). (إذا) is like the first, attached to (شدّوا). (الفاء) links the apodosis of the second condition. (الفاء) is a conjunction of ramification (li-l-tafrīʿ). (إمّا) is a particle of option (ḥarf takhyīr). (منا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, i.e.: "either you show grace (tamunnū minnan) ..." and likewise (إمّا فداء). (بعد) is an adverb indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of accusative, attached to (منّا). (حتّى) is a particle of limit and of genitive. (تضع) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied «an» after حتّى, and the interpreted maṣdar (أن تضع ... ) is in the position of genitive through (حتّى), attached to the content of the four events: the striking, the tightening of the bond, the showing of grace and the ransom. (ذلك) is a demonstrative in the position of nominative, the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: "The matter is that." (الواو) is a conjunction - or resumptive. (لو) is a non-jussive conditional particle. (اللام) links the apodosis of لو. (منهم) is attached to (انتصر), by including in it the meaning of "took revenge". (الواو) is a conjunction. (لكن) is for rectification (istidrāk) and has no governing effect. (اللام) is causal. (يبلو) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied «an» after the lām, (ببعض) is attached to (يبلو), and the interpreted maṣdar (أن يبلو ... ) is in the position of genitive through the lām, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "He commanded you thus". (الواو) is resumptive, and the (الواو) in (قتلوا) is the nāʾib fāʿil. (في سبيل) is attached to (قتلوا). (الفاء) is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar because the mubtadaʾ resembles a condition ...
The clause «لقيتم ... » is in the position of genitive, by the annexation of إذا to it «[Note: the condition, its protasis and its apodosis follow upon the preceding rulings, i.e. if the matter is as mentioned of the misguidance of the disbelievers and the expiation of the evil deeds of the believers who do good ... then when you meet ..]». The clause «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين). The clause «(اضربوا) الرقاب ضربا» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. The clause «أثخنتموهم ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi «[Note: the wāw in (أثخنتموهم) is redundant; it is the lengthening of the vowel of the mīm.]». The clause «شدّوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. The clause «(تمنّون) منّا ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause of the apodosis. The clause «(تفدون) فداء ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause (تمنون). The clause «تضع الحرب ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-type relative (the implied «an»).
The clause «(الأمر) ذلك ... » has no grammatical position, being parenthetical - or resumptive. The clause «لو يشاء الله ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumption that stands after حتّى the opening particle. The clause «انتصر منهم ... » has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. The clause «(أمركم) ليبلو» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause لو يشاء. The clause «يبلو ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-type relative (the implied «an»). The clause «الذين قتلوا ... لن يضلّ ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «قتلوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين). The clause «يضلّ ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين). The clause «سيهديهم ... » has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī). The clause «يصلح ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause سيهديهم. 6- (الواو) is a conjunction. (الجنّة) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) by extension «[Note: the original is: He will admit them into the Garden.]». (لهم) is attached to (عرّفها). The clause «يدخلهم ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause سيهديهم. The clause «عرّفها ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive «[Note: or it is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from the agent of يدخل or its object, with an implied «qad».]».

* Morphology:
(4) الوثاق: a noun for that with which captives are bound, namely the fetter or the rope; its wazn is فعال with fatḥa on the fā', and its plural is وثق with two ḍammas. (فداء) is a samāʿī (heard, non-systematic) maṣdar of the triliteral verb فدى يفدي of the باب ضرب (pattern of ضرب). In the word there is iʿlāl (weak-letter change) - or ibdāl (substitution): the weak letter, the yā', is turned into a hamza because it comes final after a silent alif; its origin is فداي ... And there are other maṣdars of the verb: فدى with fatḥa on the fā' and with kasra. (تضع) contains iʿlāl by deletion: it is a defective verb of the type mithāl (assimilated), its fā' being deleted in the imperfect, and its wazn is تعل with two fatḥas. (بعضكم) is a noun for a part or a portion or a group; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa and sukūn, and its plural is أبعاض on the pattern أفعال.

* Rhetoric:
The mursal majāz (loose figurative usage): in the words of the Exalted «فَضَرْبَ الرِّقابِ».
It is a mursal majāz for killing, and killing is expressed by it to indicate that it ought to be by striking the neck wherever possible, and to depict it in the most dreadful image, because striking the neck involves making the head fly off, which is the noblest of the body's members and the seat of its senses, and the body is left cast down in a shocking posture - we seek refuge with Allah the Exalted. The relation (ʿalāqa) of this majāz is mentioning the part and intending the whole: he mentioned the striking of the neck and meant killing.
The explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya): in the words of the Exalted «حَتَّى تَضَعَ الْحَرْبُ أَوْزارَها».
Here he borrowed "burdens" (awzār) for the implements of war and its heavy loads without which it cannot stand, such as weapons and horses. It may also be an implicit metaphor, by likening war to riding beasts carrying burdens, that is, heavy loads, while the affirmation of burdens is an imaginative attribution (takhyīl).

* Benefits:
- The rulings on jihad and captives..
The scholars differed over the ruling of this verse. Some said: it is abrogated by His words (فَإِمَّا تَثْقَفَنَّهُمْ فِي الْحَرْبِ فَشَرِّدْ بِهِمْ مَنْ خَلْفَهُمْ),
and by His words (فَاقْتُلُوا الْمُشْرِكِينَ حَيْثُ وَجَدْتُمُوهُمْ). This is the view of Qatāda, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Suddī and Ibn Jurayj. To it went al-Awzāʿī and the people of raʾy (the Ḥanafīs). They said: it is not permissible to show grace to a disbelieving captive, nor to ransom him; rather it is either killing or enslavement, whichever the imam sees fit. The author of al-Kashshāf transmitted from Mujāhid that he said: Today there is neither grace nor ransom; it is only Islam or the striking of the neck. Most scholars held that the verse is firmly established (muḥkama), and the imam has the choice, with regard to adult male disbelievers who have been captured, between killing them, enslaving them, showing them grace and releasing them without compensation, or ransoming them for money or for Muslim captives. To this went Ibn ʿUmar, and so said al-Ḥasan, ʿAṭāʾ and most of the Companions and scholars. It is the view of al-Thawrī, al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad and Isḥāq. Ibn ʿAbbās said: When the Muslims became many and their power grew strong, Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed concerning the captives (فإما منّا بعد وإما فداء). This is the sound view, because it was the practice of the Prophet ﷺ and of the caliphs after him.
On the authority of Abū Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet ﷺ sent horsemen towards Najd, and they brought a man of the Banū Ḥanīfa called Thumāma, and tied him to one of the pillars of the mosque. The Prophet ﷺ went out to him and said: What do you have, Thumāma? He said: I have good, Muḥammad. If you kill, you kill one who has blood-guilt; if you show favour, you show favour to one who is grateful; and if you want money, ask and you will be given as much of it as you wish. The Prophet ﷺ left him. The next day he said to him: What do you have, Thumāma? He said the same as his first statement. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
Release Thumāma. He went off to a palm grove near the mosque, washed, then entered the mosque and said: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger. By Allah, there was nothing on earth more hateful to me than your face, and now your face has become the most beloved of faces to me. By Allah, there was no religion more hateful to me than your religion, and now your religion has become the most beloved of all religion to me. By Allah, there was no city more hateful to me than your city, and now your city has become the most beloved of all cities to me. Your horsemen seized me while I was intending the ʿumra, so what do you think? The Prophet ﷺ gave him good news and commanded him to perform the ʿumra. When he came to Mecca, someone said to him: Have you turned apostate? He said: No, but I have become a Muslim with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. By Allah, not a grain of wheat will come to you from al-Yamāma until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ permits it. Related by al-Bukhārī and Muslim.
It is understood from His words the Exalted: حَتَّى تَضَعَ الْحَرْبُ أَوْزارَها that jihad continues until the end of time. In the hadith, his words, peace be upon him: Jihad is ongoing from the time Allah sent me until the last of my community fights the Dajjāl.

safi-cedvel:7-7.t:
* I'rab:
(أيّها) is a vocative, an indefinite noun that is specified (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of accusative. The clause «النداء ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين); the clause «تنصروا ... » has no grammatical position, being the response to the vocative; the clause «ينصركم ... » has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of the condition not joined by the fā'; and the clause «يثبّت ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause of the apodosis.

safi-cedvel:8-9.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (الفاء) is redundant (zāʾida) because the relative noun resembles a condition. (تعسا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb. (لهم) is attached to (تعسا) «[Note: the lām has the meaning of transitivity; or the preposition and its genitive noun are the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: the punishment is for them.]». (الواو) is a conjunction, and the fāʿil (agent) of (أضلّ) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to Allah, understood from the context. The clause «الذين كفروا ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين); the clause «(تعسوا) تعسا ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين); and the clause «أضلّ ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the implied clause (تعسوا). 9- The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم كرهوا..) is in the position of genitive through the «bāʾ», attached to an omitted word that is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ ذلك.
(ما) is a relative in the position of accusative, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (الفاء) is a conjunction. The clause «ذلك بأنّهم كرهوا ... » has no grammatical position, being a causal explanation of the preceding supplication «[Note: or an explanatory resumption.]». The clause «كرهوا ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of أنّ. The clause «أنزل الله ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما). The clause «أحبط ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause كرهوا.

* Morphology:
(تعسا) is a samāʿī maṣdar of the triliteral verb تعس of the باب فرح (pattern of فرح), meaning "he fell"; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa and sukūn.

* Benefits:
. The explanatory clause for the governor of the noun that has been left aside (al-ism al-mushtaghal ʿanhu).
For example: زيدا ضربته or زيدا ضربت أخاه. The clause ضربت explains the omitted verb implied before (زيد), meaning (ضربت زيدا ضربته). As for the words of the Exalted وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَتَعْساً لَهُمْ: الذين is a mubtadaʾ, and تعسا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb which is the khabar. (الذين) cannot be accusative through an omitted verb that (تعسا) explains, as you would say: زيدا ضربا إياه; and likewise it is not permissible to say: زيدا جدعا له, nor عمرا سقيا له. Rather you say with nominative: زيد جدعا له, and عمر سقيا له, because the lām is attached to the omitted verb and not to the maṣdar, since it does not govern through a preposition, and it is not the lām of reinforcement (lām al-taqwiya), because that is obligatory here, whereas the lām of reinforcement is not obligatory. And the words of the Exalted: سَلْ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ كَمْ آتَيْناهُمْ مِنْ آيَةٍ: if you take (من) to be redundant, then كم is a mubtadaʾ or a mafʿūl bihi of آتينا implied after it. And if you take it to be explicative of (كم), then it is a second mafʿūl bihi, fronted, of آتينا only. Like:
أعشرين درهما أعطيتك (Did I give you twenty dirhams?).

safi-cedvel:10-11.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for rebuking interrogation (istifhām tawbīkhī). (الفاء) is a conjunction in both places. (في الأرض) is attached to (يسيروا). (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative, the khabar of كان. (من قبلهم) is attached to an omitted word that is the ṣila of الذين. (عليهم) is attached to (دمّر), by including in it the meaning "covered" or "was angry" «[Note: in the lexicon: دمّره and دمّر عليه mean "He destroyed him" ... so there is no inclusion of meaning and no omission of an object.]», and the object of دمّر is omitted, i.e. their wealth and possessions. (الواو) is a conjunction. (للكافرين) is attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أمثالها). The clause «لم يسيروا ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e.:
"Did they stay seated and not travel" The clause «ينظروا ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause لم يسيروا. The clause «كان عاقبة ... » is in the position of accusative, the object of the verb of looking (naẓar) which is suspended by the interrogative, with an implied preposition. The clause «دمّر الله ... » has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «للكافرين أمثالها» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause دمّر الله. 11- (ذلك بأنّ الله ... ) is like «ذلك بأنّهم» «[Note: in verse (9) of this sūra.]». (لا) is the lā of generic negation (nāfiya li-l-jins). (لهم) is attached to the khabar of لا ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الكافرين ... ) is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the first interpreted maṣdar in i'rab and in attachment. The clause «ذلك بأنّ الله ... » has no grammatical position, being a causal explanation of what precedes - or an explanatory resumption. The clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «لا مولى لهم ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of أنّ.

safi-cedvel:12-12.t:
* I'rab:
(جنّات) is a second mafʿūl bihi by extension «[Note: the original is: He admits those who believe into gardens ...]», accusative, its sign of accusative being the kasra. (من تحتها) is attached to (تجري) «[Note: or attached to a ḥāl from الأنهار.]», with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. from beneath its trees. (الواو) is a conjunction in all three places. (ما) is a maṣdar particle ... (لهم) is attached to an adjective (naʿt) of (مثوى). The interpreted maṣdar (ما تأكل الأنعام) is in the position of genitive through the kāf, attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq whose governor is يأكلون. The clause «إنّ الله يدخل ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «يدخل ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of إنّ. The clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين). The clause «عملوا ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the ṣila clause. The clause «تجري ... » is in the position of accusative, an adjective of جنّات. The clause «الذين كفروا ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause. The clause «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين). The clause «يتمتّعون ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين). The clause «يأكلون» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يتمتّعون. The clause «تأكل الأنعام» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-type relative (ما). The clause «النار مثوى لهم» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Rhetoric:
The simile (al-tashbīh): in the words of the Exalted «وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا يَتَمَتَّعُونَ وَيَأْكُلُونَ كَما تَأْكُلُ الْأَنْعامُ وَالنَّارُ مَثْوىً لَهُمْ».
Here the disbelievers are likened to cattle in taking enjoyment through eating: they eat out of greed and voracity, as is the way of beasts, in contempt of them and belittling of their state, describing them as base and gluttonous, qualities which the Arabs censure and hate.

safi-cedvel:36-38.t:
* I'rab:
The clause: «إنّما الحياة ... لعب» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya).
The clause: «تؤمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause: «تتّقوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to «تؤمنوا».
The clause: «يؤتكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) not preceded by the fāʾ.
The clause: «يسألكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the apodosis clause.
37- (الواو) in (يسألكموها) is redundant (zāʾida); it is the lengthening of the vowel of the mīm. (الفاء) is a conjunction. (يحفكم) is an imperfect verb, jussive, conjoined to the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). The agent (fāʿil) of (يخرج) is a pronoun referring to the miserliness understood from His words (تبخلوا), the apodosis.
The clause: «يسألكموها ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī), or a causal clause.
The clause: «يحفكم» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «يسألكموها».
The clause: «تبخلوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis not preceded by the fāʾ.
The clause: «يخرج ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the apodosis.
38- (هؤلاء) is a demonstrative in the position of nominative as the predicate (khabar) of the subject (mubtadaʾ) (أنتم) [Note: or it is a vocative from which the vocative particle has been omitted, and the clause «تدعون» is the predicate of the mubtadaʾ «أنتم».], and (الواو) in (تدعون) is the deputy agent (nāʾib al-fāʿil). (اللام) is for causation. (تنفقوا) is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām. (في سبيل) is attached to (تنفقوا).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تنفقوا ... ) is in the position of genitive through the lām, attached to (تدعون).
(الفاء) is a conjunction. (منكم) is attached to a fronted predicate of the postponed mubtadaʾ (من), a relative noun. (الواو) is resumptive. (من), the second, is a jussive conditional noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. (الفاء) is the particle linking the apodosis. (إنّما) is the restrictive particle combined with what restricts it (kāffa and makfūfa). (عن نفسه) is attached to (يبخل). (الواو) is parenthetical, and a conjunction in the two following places. (تتولّوا) is an imperfect verb, jussive, the protasis ... and the wāw is the agent. (غيركم) is an adjective (naʿt) of (قوما), accusative. (لا) is negative. (يكونوا) is a defective imperfect verb (kāna and its sisters), jussive, conjoined to (يستبدل). (أمثالكم) is the predicate of (يكونوا), accusative.
The clause: «أنتم هؤلاء ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause: «تدعون» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
The clause: «تنفقوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-type relative (أن), which is implied.
The clause: «منكم من يبخل ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «تدعون».
The clause: «يبخل ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause: «من يبخل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause: «يبخل ... » is in the position of nominative as the predicate of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: it is permissible for the predicate to be the protasis clause and the apodosis clause together.].
The clause: «إنّما يبخل عن نفسه» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, preceded by the fāʾ.
The clause: «الله الغنيّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical.
The clause: «أنتم الفقراء ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the parenthetical clause.
The clause: «تتولّوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the conditional clause «من يبخل ...»
or to the conditional clause «إن تؤمنوا».
The clause: «يستبدل ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis not preceded by the fāʾ.
The clause: «لا يكونوا أمثالكم» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «يستبدل».

safi-cedvel:13-13.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (كأيّن) a figurative expression for a number meaning "many", indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject) (من قرية) tamyīz (specification) of the figurative number (قوّة) tamyīz of (أشدّ), (من قريتك) attached to أشدّ (التي) a relative noun in the position of genitive, naʿt (adjective) of قريتك (الفاء) conjunction (لا) the lā of generic negation (لهم) attached to the khabar (predicate) of لا.
Clause: «كأيّن من قرية ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
Clause: «هي أشدّ ...» is in the position of genitive, naʿt of قرية.
Clause: «أخرجتك ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (التي).
Clause: «أهلكناهم ...» is in the position of nominative, khabar of كأيّن.
Clause: «لا ناصر لهم» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause of the khabar [Note: The meaning: We destroyed them, and no helper helped them; so it is a report about what has passed ...].

* Benefits:
- كأيّن..
It is a compound noun made of the kāf of comparison and the tanwīn-bearing ayy; hence it is permissible to pause on it with the nūn, because the tanwīn, once it entered the compound, came to resemble an original nūn, and for this reason it is written in the muṣḥaf as a nūn. Whoever pauses on it by dropping it treats it according to its original ruling, which is dropping in pausal form.
And (كأي) agrees with (كم) in several matters..
Initial position in the sentence, and conveying multitude - in most cases - as in His saying, the Exalted: وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ هِيَ أَشَدُّ قُوَّةً مِنْ قَرْيَتِكَ الَّتِي أَخْرَجَتْكَ أَهْلَكْناهُمْ فَلا ناصِرَ لَهُمْ. As for the interrogative use, it is extremely rare, as in the saying of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb to Ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with them both: (كأين تقرأ سورة الأحزاب آية؟) (How many verses do you recite of Sūrat al-Aḥzāb?) He said: Seventy-three.
And it differs from it in five matters: 1- It is compound whereas kam is not compound..
2- Its tamyīz is mostly genitive through min, and so it occurs in the Noble Qur'an: (وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ نَبِيٍّ) and (كَأَيِّنْ مِنْ آيَةٍ) and (وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ).
3- According to the majority it does not occur as interrogative, but only as declarative.
4- It does not occur in the genitive.
5- Its khabar does not occur as a single word but as a clause.

safi-cedvel:14-14.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) interrogative of denial (الفاء) resumptive (من) a relative noun in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject) (على بيّنة) attached to the khabar of كان (من ربّه) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (بيّنة), (كمن) attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, the first (من) (له) attached to (زيّن).
Clause: «من كان على بيّنة ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
Clause: «كان على بيّنة ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative noun (من).
Clause: «زيّن له سوء ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the second relative noun (من).
Clause: «اتّبعوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the second ṣila clause.

safi-cedvel:15-15.t:
[Note: There are many interpretations of the i'rab of this verse from the earlier i'rab scholars, and we have preferred the clearest, easiest and least interpretive of these analyses.]
* I'rab:
(مثل) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, its khabar (predicate) omitted, that is: "in what is recited to you is the likeness of Paradise" - or "the likeness of Paradise is what you recite" - (التي) a relative noun in the position of genitive, naʿt (adjective) of الجنّة, the returning pronoun being omitted (المتّقون) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) (فيها) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أنهار) (من ماء) attached to a naʿt of (أنهار) (الواو) a conjunction in the six places (من لبن) attached to a naʿt of the second (أنهار) (من خمر) naʿt of the third (أنهار) (للشاربين) attached to (لذّة) (من عسل) naʿt of the fourth (أنهار) (لهم) attached to a fronted khabar, the mubtadaʾ being implied, that is: "kinds" [Note: Or "pairs", taken from the noble verse: فيهما من كلّ فاكهة زوجان.], (فيها) attached to the settling (istiqrār) which is the khabar (من كلّ) attached to a naʿt of the implied mubtadaʾ (مغفرة) conjoined to the implied mubtadaʾ (من ربّهم) attached to a naʿt of (مغفرة) (كمن) attached to the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being:
"Is he who is in this bliss like him who abides ..." [Note: Or: the likeness of this described reward is like the reward of one who abides ... but in this there is additional interpretation.
It is also possible that the preposition and its genitive noun (كمن) ... are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ مثل الجنّة ... and what lies between them is parenthetical.], (في النار) attached to (خالد), and (الواو) in (سقوا) is the nāʾib fāʿil (ما) direct object (mafʿūl bihi), accusative.
Clause: «مثل الجنّة ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
Clause: «وعد المتّقون ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative noun (التي).
Clause: «فيها أنهار» has no grammatical position, explanatory resumption [Note: Or it is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ مثل الجنّة, and the absence of a linking pronoun does not prevent this because the khabar is the very same as the mubtadaʾ.].
Clause: «لم يتغيّر طعمه» is in the position of genitive, naʿt of لبن.
Clause: «لهم فيها (أصناف) ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause فيها أنهار.
Clause: «(أمن هو في نعيم) كمن هو خالد» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
Clause: «هو خالد ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative noun (من).
Clause: «سقوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause [Note: Or it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) with an implied (قد).].
Clause: «قطّع ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause سقوا.

* Morphology:
(آسن) an active participle from the triliteral (أسن), its wazn is فاعل, with a madda substituted for the hamza and the alif of فاعل..
(طعم) the name of what the taste perceives of sweetness or bitterness; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn; its plural is طعوم with two ḍammas. (عسل) the name of the known food substance; it is both masculine and feminine, and in the noble verse it occurs as masculine, being described as purified; its wazn is فعل with two fatḥas, and a verb is derived from it, so one says ʿasila al-ṭaʿām - with fatḥa on the mīm [Translator's note: the source says "mīm", but the verb quoted has no mīm; the sense is the middle letter] - meaning "he made it into honey", from the bābs naṣara and ḍaraba.
(مصفّى) a passive participle from the four-letter verb ṣaffā; its wazn is مفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn.
(سقوا) it contains an i'lāl by making sākin and an i'lāl by omission; its original is suqiyū - with ḍamma on the yāʾ - the ḍamma on the yāʾ was found heavy and so it was made sākin - i'lāl by sukūn - and its vowel was transferred to the qāf.. the yāʾ and the wāw met as two sākin letters, so the yāʾ - the lām of the word - was dropped, which is an i'lāl by omission, and it became سقوا; its wazn is فعوا with two ḍammas.
(أمعاء) the plural of maʿan - with kasra on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn followed by an alif - the name of the intestines of the belly; its wazn is فعل, and the alif is converted from a yāʾ, because the dual is maʿayān.. and the (hamza) in the plural is converted from a yāʾ because it came at the end after a sākin alif.. or it is the plural of maʿy, whose wazn is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn followed by a yāʾ; both al-maʿā and al-maʿy are masculine and may be feminine.

safi-cedvel:16-16.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (منهم) attached to the fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من), (إليك) attached to (يستمع), (حتّى) a particle of commencement (من عندك) attached to (خرجوا), (للذين) attached to (قالوا), (العلم) direct object, accusative (ماذا) an interrogative noun in the position of accusative, fronted object [Note: Or (ما) is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ, whose khabar is the relative noun (ذا), the clause قال being the ṣila of the relative noun, and the quoted speech omitted, which is the returning pronoun.], (آنفا) a ḥāl, accusative, that is: "beginning" [Note: It is possible that it is an adverb attached to (قال), that is: "what did he say just now ..."], (على قلوبهم) attached to (طبع).
Clause: «منهم من يستمع» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
Clause: «يستمع إليك ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative noun (من).
Clause: «خرجوا ...» is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position, apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
Clause: «أوتوا العلم ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
Clause: «قال ...» is in the position of accusative, quoted speech of the verb قالوا. Clause: «أولئك الذين ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
Clause: «طبع الله ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
Clause: «اتّبعوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.

* Morphology:
(آنفا) an active participle from the triliteral (أنف), which is an unused verb, and the madda is a substitute for the hamza and the alif ...

safi-cedvel:17-17.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (اهتدوا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied ḍamma on the omitted alif because of the meeting of two sākin letters (هدى) second direct object (mafʿūl bihi). Clause: «الذين اهتدوا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
Clause: «اهتدوا ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
Clause: «زادهم ...» is in the position of nominative, khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (الذين).
Clause: «آتاهم ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause زادهم.

safi-cedvel:18-18.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive (هل) an interrogative particle containing the sense of negation, and the pronoun in (ينظرون) refers back to the unbelievers of Mecca (إلّا) for restriction (بغتة) a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of ḥāl (circumstantial) [Note: Or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the verbal noun because it meets it in meaning ... "it comes to them" in the sense of "it takes them by surprise".], (الفاء) causal (قد) a particle of affirmation..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تأتيهم) is in the position of accusative, badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) for الساعة, that is:
"They await the coming of the Hour."
(الفاء) resumptive - or a conjunction - (أنّى) an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as an adverb, attached to the fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ذكراهم) [Note: It is possible that (ذكراهم) is the agent of the verb جاءتهم ... in which case the mubtadaʾ is implied, that is: "how could deliverance be for them ..."], (لهم) attached to the settling (istiqrār) which is the khabar (إذا) an adverb of future time devoid of condition, and the agent of (جاءتهم) is a pronoun referring back to the Hour.
Clause: «ينظرون ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive [Note: It is possible that the clause is conjoined to the resumptive clause: أولئك الذين طبع الله ... (verse 16) with what lies between them being parenthetical.].
Clause: «تأتيهم ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the maṣdar particle (أن).
Clause: «جاء أشراطها» has no grammatical position, causal.
Clause: «أنّى لهم ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
Clause: «جاءتهم ...» is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.

* Morphology:
(أشراطها) the plural of sharaṭ, whose wazn is فعل with two fatḥas, meaning a sign; the wazn of أشراط is أفعال, like sabab and asbāb.

* Benefits:
- The signs of the Hour..
This verse alluded to the coming of the signs of the Hour in His saying, the Exalted: فَهَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا السَّاعَةَ أَنْ تَأْتِيَهُمْ بَغْتَةً فَقَدْ جاءَ أَشْراطُها. Since the matter of the Hour is felt by souls to be slow in coming, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned that it will come suddenly and that some of its marks and signs have already occurred. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned this in many of his sound hadiths. We shall cite some for clarification:
From Sahl ibn Saʿd, who said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say, with his finger, thus - the middle one and the one next to the thumb - and say: "I was sent, and the Hour, like these two."
It was said that its meaning is that what lies between his being sent ﷺ and the rising of the Hour is like what lies between these two fingers in difference of length, so it is a small thing. It was also said: it is an indication of near proximity.
From Anas, who said near his death: Shall I not tell you a hadith from the Prophet ﷺ that no one other than me will tell you? I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Among the signs of the Hour are that knowledge will be taken away and ignorance will appear (ignorance of the Law and religion), wine will be drunk, fornication will spread, the men will go and the women remain, until there will be one guardian for fifty women."
From Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Among the signs of the Hour are that time will draw close, knowledge will diminish, trials will appear, miserliness will be cast, and harj will increase." They said: What is harj?
He said: "Killing."
And from Abū Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: A Bedouin asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: When is the Hour? He ﷺ said: "When trust is lost, then wait for the Hour." He said:
And what is the loss of trust? He said: "When a matter is entrusted to those who are not fit for it."
The scholars said: among the signs of the Hour is the splitting of the moon, as proved by His saying, the Exalted: اقْتَرَبَتِ السَّاعَةُ وَانْشَقَّ الْقَمَرُ

safi-cedvel:19-19.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition (لا) the lā of generic negation (إلّا) for exception (الله) the name of Majesty, badal (substitute) for the latent pronoun in the khabar (predicate) (لذنبك) attached to (استغفر), and likewise (للمؤمنين) with an omitted muḍāf (first term of a construct), that is: "for the sin of the believers" ...
(الواو) resumptive, and the interpreted maṣdar (أنّه لا اله إلّا الله) is in the position of accusative, standing in for the two objects of اعلم. Clause: «اعلم ...» has no grammatical position, apodosis of an implied condition: if you have known the happiness of the believers and the wretchedness of the unbelievers, then take the knowledge of the oneness of Allah.
Clause: «لا إله إلّا الله» is in the position of nominative, khabar of أنّ.
Clause: «استغفر ...» is conjoined to the clause اعلم.
Clause: «الله يعلم ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
Clause: «يعلم ...» is in the position of nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (الله).

* Morphology:
(متقلّبكم) a maṣdar mīmī (verbal noun with prefixed mīm) of the five-letter verb taqallaba; its wazn is متفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the doubled ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:20-21.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (لولا) a particle of urging (الفاء) conjunction, and likewise the wāw (فيها) attached to (ذكر), (في قلوبهم) attached to the fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (مرض) (إليك) attached to (ينظرون), (نظر) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (عليه) in the place of the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the passive participle المغشيّ (من الموت) attached to (المغشيّ) (الفاء) resumptive (أولى) mubtadaʾ [Note: It is possible that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "destruction" or "punishment is for them" ... that is: nearer and closer..
Al-Aṣmaʿī alone made it a past verb whose agent is a pronoun indicated by the context, that is: "what destroys him came near him", and al-Mubarrad and al-Zamakhsharī followed him in that.], nominative, its khabar being (طاعة) [Note: Or its khabar is (لهم), and the meaning: destruction is for them, because (أولى) is from "woe" ... in which case (طاعة) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "our command is obedience".. or it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being "better for you" or "from us is obedience"], (لهم) attached to (أولى) [Note: And the lām has the meaning of the bāʾ, that is: "obedience and a fair word are more fitting for them".].
Clause: «يقول الذين ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
Clause: «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
Clause: «لولا نزّلت سورة» is in the position of accusative, quoted speech.
Clause: «أنزلت سورة» is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «ذكر فيها القتال» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause أنزلت.
Clause: «رأيت ...» has no grammatical position, apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
Clause: «في قلوبهم مرض ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
Clause: «ينظرون ...» is in the position of accusative, ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative noun.
Clause: «أولى لهم» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
21- (الفاء) resumptive, and the second is a linker of the apodosis (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle (اللام) occurring in the apodosis of لو, and the noun of (كان) is a latent pronoun referring back to the truthfulness and faith understood from the context (لهم) attached to (خيرا).
Clause: «عزم الأمر ...» is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «لو صدقوا ...» has no grammatical position, apodosis of a non-jussive condition (إذا).
Clause: «كان خيرا لهم» has no grammatical position, apodosis of a non-jussive condition (لو).

* Morphology:
(20) نظر: a samāʿī (heard, not rule-based) maṣdar of the triliteral naẓara, bāb naṣara; its wazn is فعل with two fatḥas.
(المغشيّ) a passive participle from the triliteral ghashiya; the original of its wazn is مفعول, then an i'lāl by substitution occurred in it; its original is maghshūy - with a yāʾ at the end - the wāw and the yāʾ met, the first being sākin, so the wāw was changed to yāʾ and merged with the other yāʾ, then the shīn was given kasra to suit the yāʾ.
(أولى) see verse (68) of Sūrat Āl ʿImrān ... in this case it is derived from al-walī, which is nearness, and its wazn is أفعل; it was also said that it is derived from al-wayl ("woe"), so its wazn is أفلع.

* Benefits:
- What may be either mubtadaʾ or khabar..
In this verse occurs His saying, the Exalted: طاعَةٌ وَقَوْلٌ مَعْرُوفٌ. It is permissible to parse طاعة as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, the implied form being: "our command is obedience". It may also be parsed as a mubtadaʾ, the implied form being: "obedience and a fair word are better". This occurs in the Noble Qur'an in several places, which we shall point out:
1- This is frequent after the fāʾ, as in His saying, the Exalted: فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ، فَعِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ، فَمَا اسْتَيْسَرَ مِنَ الْهَدْيِ، (فَنَظِرَةٌ إِلى مَيْسَرَةٍ). If they are parsed as khabars, the implied form is: "what is obligatory is such-and-such"; if as mubtadaʾs, the implied form is: "then upon him is such-and-such", or "then upon you is such-and-such".
2- It also occurs elsewhere, as in His saying, the Exalted: فَصَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ, that is: "my course is" or "a fair patience is better"; and His saying, the Exalted: طاعَةٌ وَقَوْلٌ مَعْرُوفٌ, that is: "our command" or "better". The first is supported by his saying:
فقالت على اسم الله أمرك طاعة ... وإن كنت قد كلفت ما لم أعوّد
(She said: In the name of Allah, your command is obeyed ... even if I have been charged with what I am not accustomed to)
The point of evidence is his saying (أمرك طاعة), which favours its being a khabar rather than a mubtadaʾ, because the poet took (طاعة) as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أمرك), and it was stated explicitly; so if we want to supply an implied form, we supply it in the light of what is stated explicitly.

safi-cedvel:22-22.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive (هل) an interrogative particle (تولّيتم) a past verb in the position of jussive, protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) (في الأرض) attached to (تفسدوا), (تقطّعوا) an imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined to (تفسدوا) by the wāw..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تفسدوا) is in the position of accusative, khabar of عسيتم. Clause: «عسيتم ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
Clause: «تولّيتم ...» has no grammatical position, parenthetical.. and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.
Clause: «تفسدوا ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the maṣdar particle (أن).
Clause: «تقطّعوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تفسدوا.

* Rhetoric:
Iltifāt (shift of person): in His saying, the Exalted «فَهَلْ عَسَيْتُمْ إِنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ».
The speech has been moved from the third person to direct address, in the manner of iltifāt, so as to be more eloquent in confirming the reproach and intensifying the rebuke.

safi-cedvel:23-23.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) a conjunction, and likewise (الواو), and the agent of (أصمّهم، أعمى) is a pair of pronouns referring back to the name of Majesty (Allah)..
Clause: «أولئك الذين ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
Clause: «لعنهم الله ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
Clause: «أصمّهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
Clause: «أعمى ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أصمّهم.

safi-cedvel:24-24.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) interrogative of reproach (الفاء) a conjunction - or resumptive - (لا) negative (أم) munqaṭiʿa (disconnected), meaning "rather" (على قلوب) attached to the fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (أقفالها).
Clause: «لا يتدبّرون ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied resumption, that is:
"Are they heedless, so that they do not ponder ..." - or it is resumptive.
Clause: «على قلوب أقفالها ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(أقفال) the plural of qufl, the name of the known device, used figuratively; its wazn is فعل with ḍamma then sukūn; there are other plurals: aqful with fatḥa on the hamza and ḍamma on the fāʾ, and qufūl with two ḍammas.

* Rhetoric:
Indefiniteness (tankīr): in His saying, the Exalted «أَمْ عَلى قُلُوبٍ أَقْفالُها».
The hearts are made indefinite, either to magnify their condition and make their matter appear dreadful, by leaving their affair vague in hardness and ignorance, as if it were said: "upon hearts of a strange kind, whose state is not known and whose measure in hardness cannot be gauged"; or because what is meant are the hearts of some of them, namely the hypocrites. The annexation of the locks indicates that they are locks specific to them, fitting to them, not of the same kind as other familiar locks.
So in the speech there is isti'āra (metaphor): their hearts are likened to chests, and something of the chests' attributes is borrowed for them, namely the locks specific to them, to suggest the improbability of their opening and the continuance of their being shut.

safi-cedvel:25-28.t:
* I'rab:
(على أدبارهم) attached to (ارتدّوا), (من بعد) attached to (ارتدّوا), (ما) a maṣdar particle (لهم) attached to (تبيّن) ...
The interpreted maṣdar (ما تبيّن..) is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The second (لهم) is attached to (سوّل), and the third (لهم) is attached to (أملى).
Clause: «إنّ الذين ارتدّوا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
Clause: «ارتدّوا ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
Clause: «تبيّن لهم الهدى ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the maṣdar particle (ما).
Clause: «الشيطان سوّل ...» is in the position of nominative, khabar of inna.
Clause: «سوّل لهم ...» is in the position of nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الشيطان).
Clause: «أملى لهم» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause سوّل.
26- The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم قالوا ... ) is in the position of genitive through the bāʾ, attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ذلك).
(للذين) attached to (قالوا), (ما) a relative noun in the position of accusative, direct object, the returning pronoun being omitted (في بعض) attached to (نطيعكم), (الواو) circumstantial..
Clause: «ذلك بأنّهم قالوا ...» has no grammatical position, causal.
Clause: «قالوا ...» is in the position of nominative, khabar of anna.
Clause: «كرهوا ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
Clause: «نزّل الله ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
Clause: «سنطيعكم ...» is in the position of accusative, quoted speech.
Clause: «الله يعلم ...» is in the position of accusative, ḥāl (circumstantial).
Clause: «يعلم ...» is in the position of nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
27- (الفاء) resumptive (كيف) an interrogative noun in the position of nominative, khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "their state" [Note: Or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, governed by an implied verb, that is: "how will they act".], (إذا) an adverb of future time devoid of condition, in the position of accusative, attached to the implied mubtadaʾ [Note: Or attached to the implied verb.].
Clause: «كيف (حالهم) ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
Clause: «توفّتهم الملائكة ...» is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «يضربون ...» is in the position of accusative, ḥāl from "the angels" or from the object.
28- (ذلك بأنّهم..) like the first [Note: In verse (26) of this sūra.] (ما) a relative noun, direct object (الله) the name of Majesty, direct object (الفاء) a conjunction.
Clause: «ذلك بأنّهم ...» has no grammatical position, causal.
Clause: «اتّبعوا ...» is in the position of nominative, khabar of inna.
Clause: «أسخط ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
Clause: «كرهوا ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause اتّبعوا.
Clause: «أحبط ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause كرهوا.

* Morphology:
(أملى) the alif is written as an undotted yāʾ because it is the fourth letter, despite being converted from a wāw, for its triliteral is malā yamlū, and al-malāwa is a span of time ...
(26) إسرار: a qiyāsī (rule-based) maṣdar of the four-letter verb asarra; its wazn is إفعال with kasra on the hamza.

safi-cedvel:29-31.t:
* I'rab:
(أم) munqaṭiʿa (disconnected), meaning "rather" plus the hamza (في قلوبهم) attached to the fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (مرض) (أن) lightened from the heavy (أنّ), its noun being an omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn).
Clause: «حسب الذين ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
Clause: «في قلوبهم مرض ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
Clause: «لن يخرج الله ...» is in the position of nominative, khabar of anna.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن لن يخرج الله ... ) is in the position of accusative, standing in for the two objects of حسب.
30- (الواو) conjunction (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle (اللام) occurring in the apodosis of لو in both places, and (الفاء) a conjunction (بسيما) attached to (عرفتهم), (الواو) a conjunction, and the third (اللام) is the lām of oath, for an implied oath (تعرفنّهم) an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of nominative (في لحن) attached to (تعرفنّ), the preposition being causal, (الواو) resumptive.
Clause: «نشاء ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
Clause: «أريناكهم ...» has no grammatical position, apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
Clause: «عرفتهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause of the apodosis.
Clause: «تعرفنّهم ...» has no grammatical position, answer to the implied oath ... and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
Clause: «الله يعلم ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
Clause: «يعلم أعمالكم» is in the position of nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
31- (الواو) conjunction (لنبلونّكم) like لتعرفنّهم (حتّى) a particle of limit and of genitive (نعلم) an imperfect verb, accusative through an implied أن after حتّى.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن نعلم) is in the position of genitive through (حتّى), attached to (نبلونّكم).
(منكم) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from المجاهدين (الواو) a conjunction in both places (نبلو) an imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined to (نعلم).
Clause: «نبلونّكم ...» has no grammatical position, answer to the implied oath ... and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position, conjoined to the first implied oath clause.
Clause: «نعلم ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the implied maṣdar particle (أن). Clause: «نبلو ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause نعلم

* Morphology:
(أضغانهم) the plural of ḍighn, a noun meaning rancour; its wazn is فعل with kasra then sukūn, and the plural is أفعال.
(أخبار) the plural of khabar.. the name of a narrated report; its wazn is فعل with two fatḥas, and the wazn of أخبار is أفعال.
(لحن) a maṣdar of the triliteral laḥana, meaning "he erred in speech", or it is a noun meaning "import", or "error in speech"; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
Isti'āra taṣrīḥiyya (explicit metaphor): in His saying, the Exalted «أَمْ حَسِبَ الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ أَنْ لَنْ يُخْرِجَ اللَّهُ أَضْغانَهُمْ».
The sickness of the soul is likened to bodily sickness, since each ruins a person and spoils his life. Here the thing compared-to is stated explicitly without the thing compared, and the metaphor is more eloquent because bodily diseases are visible to the eye, their effect apparent.

safi-cedvel:32-32.t:
* I'rab:
(عن سبيل) attached to (صدّوا) by implying the meaning "they turned away" (من بعد) attached to (شاقّوا), (ما) a maṣdar particle.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما تبيّن..) is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
(لهم) attached to (تبيّن), (شيئا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the verbal noun, that is: "any harm" (الواو) a conjunction.
Clause: «إنّ الذين كفروا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
Clause: «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
Clause: «صدّوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
Clause: «شاقّوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
Clause: «تبيّن لهم الهدى» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the maṣdar particle (ما).
Clause: «لن يضرّوا ...» is in the position of nominative, khabar of inna.
Clause: «سيحبط ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the khabar of inna.

safi-cedvel:33-33.t:
* I'rab:
(أيّها) a vocative, a specific indefinite noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of accusative (الذين) in the position of accusative, badal (substitute) for أيّ - or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to it - (الواو) a conjunction (لا) prohibitive, jussive-governing ...
Clause: «النداء ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
Clause: «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
Clause: «أطيعوا الله ...» has no grammatical position, answer to the vocative.
Clause: «أطيعوا الرسول ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause answering the vocative.
Clause: «لا تبطلوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause answering the vocative.

safi-cedvel:34-34.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ الذين ... سبيل الله) its i'rab has already been given [Note: In verse (32), word by word and clause by clause.], (ثمّ) a conjunction (الواو) circumstantial (الفاء) redundant (zāʾida), because of the resemblance of the relative noun, the noun of inna, to a condition (لهم) attached to (يغفر).
Clause: «ماتوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause كفروا ...
Clause: «هم كفّار ...» is in the position of accusative, ḥāl (circumstantial).
Clause: «لن يغفر الله لهم» is in the position of nominative, khabar (predicate) of inna.

safi-cedvel:35-35.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) linking the apodosis of the implied condition (لا) prohibitive, jussive-governing (الواو) a conjunction (تدعوا) an imperfect verb, jussive, conjoined to (تهنوا), (إلى السلم) attached to (تدعوا), (الواو) circumstantial, the second resumptive, and the third a conjunction ... (معكم) an adverb, accusative, attached to the khabar (predicate).
Clause: «تهنوا ...» has no grammatical position, apodosis of an implied condition, that is: if you meet the unbelievers, do not weaken ... or: if you know that jihad is obligatory, do not weaken.
Clause: «تدعوا ...» is conjoined to the clause تهنوا.
Clause: «أنتم الأعلون» is in the position of accusative, ḥāl (circumstantial).
Clause: «الله معكم» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
Clause: «لن يتركم ...» is conjoined to the clause الله معكم.

* Morphology:
(يتركم) it contains an i'lāl by omission; its original is yawtirukum, so it is a weak verb of the mithāl type whose fāʾ is dropped in the imperfect; its wazn is يعلكم.

* Benefits:
- مع..
1- It is a noun, as proved by the tanwīn in your saying (معا), and making its ʿayn sākin is the dialect of Ghanm and Rabīʿa, and the saying of al-Naḥḥās that it is a particle is rejected. It is used in the construct state, in which case it is an adverb, and it then has three meanings:
1- The place of gathering, hence it is predicated of persons, as in His saying, the Exalted, in the verse at hand: وَاللَّهُ مَعَكُمْ.
2- The time of it: (جئت مع العصر) (I came at ʿaṣr time) ..
3- Synonymous with (عند), as in the reading of some: (هذا ذكر من معي).
2- It may be used on its own, in which case it takes tanwīn, and is a ḥāl; and it has occurred as an adverb used as a predicate, as in the saying of Jandal ibn ʿAmr:
أفيقوا بني حرب وأهواؤنا معا ... وأرماحنا موصولة لم تقضب
(Come to your senses, sons of Ḥarb, while our desires are together ... and our spears are joined, not broken off)
It was also said that (معا) is a ḥāl and the khabar is omitted..
Used on its own it means "jamʿan" (all together) according to Ibn Mālik, which is contrary to the saying of Thaʿlab: if you say "they came jamīʿan", it could mean that they acted at one time or at two times, whereas if you say "they came maʿan" the time is one.
Maʿan is used for a group as it is used for two. Mutammim ibn Nuwayra said:
يذكّرون ذا البث الحزين ببثهّ ... إذا حنت الأولى سجعن لها معا
(They remind the sorrowful one of his sorrow ... when the first yearns, they coo in response to her together)
And al-Khansāʾ said:
وأفنى رجالي فبادوا معا ... فأصبح قلبي بهم مستفزّا
(He destroyed my men and they perished together ... so my heart over them has become shaken)
